sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Swarajya vs. Samrajya**: The shift from Shivaji’s defensive, localized **Swarajya** to the Peshwa-led **Samrajya** (pan-Indian empire) necessitated a shift from guerrilla warfare to conventional military dominance.
• **Fiscal Mechanism**: The expansion was fueled by **Chauth** (1/4th of revenue for protection) and **Sardeshmukhi** (additional 1/10th as hereditary right), creating a 'tributary' rather than 'administrative' empire.
• **Confederacy Model**: The Maratha state evolved into a **Confederacy** (Peshwa, Gaekwad, Holkar, Scindia, Bhonsle) to manage vast territories, leading to decentralized power.
• **Key Factor**: The **Mobile Military State** model allowed Marathas to project power rapidly across the subcontinent, though it lacked a centralized bureaucratic integration.

items.definition: A tax levied on non-Maratha territories to prevent Maratha raids; essentially 'protection money' that legitimized Maratha influence.
An additional levy of 10% claimed by the Maratha ruler as the 'Sardeshmukh' (chief headman) of the entire Deccan, asserting superior sovereignty.
Originally the Prime Minister, the office became hereditary under Balaji Vishwanath, effectively shifting power from the Chhatrapati to the Peshwa.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **The 'Strike at the Trunk' Policy**: Baji Rao I’s strategy to attack the Mughal center (Delhi) to cause the collapse of the branches (provinces).
• **Military Innovation**: Integration of Gardi (infantry trained in European style) to counter traditional cavalry limitations.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of a unified administrative structure, internal rivalry among confederate chiefs, and failure to win over local populations (e.g., Jats, Rajputs).
• **Solutions**: The need for a centralized revenue system and a cohesive political ideology beyond mere plunder.

items.title: Mnemonic for Confederacy Families
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-S-H-B-P'
• **Decoded Meaning**: Gaekwad (Baroda), Scindia (Gwalior), Holkar (Indore), Bhonsle (Nagpur), Peshwa (Pune).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Confederacy' with a 'Unified Empire'. The Maratha state was a loose confederation of chiefs, not a centralized bureaucratic state like the Mughals.

Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Fiscal-Military State' to describe the Maratha expansion. It highlights how their military success was inextricably linked to their innovative, albeit predatory, revenue collection methods.

keyTakeaways: Maratha expansion shifted from defensive guerrilla warfare to offensive cavalry-led imperial expansion.
The Confederacy model allowed for rapid territorial gains but prevented long-term administrative consolidation.
The reliance on Chauth and Sardeshmukhi created a tributary relationship that alienated local populations and hindered state-building.
